question.text: Masala bonds are best described as:

answer.text: Corporate bonds issued outside India by Indian companies, denominated in Indian rupees
Government bonds issued by the RBI for domestic investors only
Zero coupon bonds issued by foreign governments in US dollars
Equity shares of Indian companies listed on foreign stock exchanges

explanation.text: The Logic: Masala bonds are corporate bonds issued outside India by Indian companies and denominated in Indian rupees. Foreign investors are eligible to invest in these bonds, and because the bonds are rupee-denominated, the currency risk from any rupee depreciation is borne by the foreign investor rather than the Indian issuer. The Trap: Masala bonds are not government bonds (option B), they are not denominated in dollars (option C), and they are debt rather than equity (option D). Note: Because masala bonds are rupee-denominated, the foreign investor bears the currency risk; this is the key distinction from foreign-currency-denominated bonds issued abroad by Indian companies.
